utterance: Hi Chloe. I see you've been having some burning when you pass urine since yesterday. Can you tell me a bit more about what's been happening? Are you also needing to go more often or urgently?
reply: It stings and burns, worst right at the end of weeing. I'm going constantly — every half hour — and only a little bit comes out. I have to rush. It's been like this since yesterday morning. The urine is a bit cloudy and smells, but I haven't seen any blood.

awards.label: How long the symptoms have been present
Colour of the urine or any visible blood

utterance: That sounds really uncomfortable. Have you had any fevers, chills, nausea, or pain in your back or sides?
reply: No, I haven't had any fevers, chills or nausea. I feel fine apart from the burning when I wee. I don't have any pain in my back or sides, just a bit of an ache low down in my tummy.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Fever, sweats, chills or shaking
Red flag excluded: Pain in the back or sides (loins)
Red flag excluded: Nausea, vomiting or feeling generally unwell

utterance: That's reassuring that you don't have fevers or back pain. Have you noticed any vaginal discharge or itchiness? And you mentioned this is a UTI 'again' - how many times have you had this before, and when was the last time?
reply: No, I haven't noticed any vaginal discharge or itchiness. I had one UTI about two years ago, that's it.

utterance: Are you currently sexually active, and have there been any new partners recently? Also, is there any chance you could be pregnant, or have you missed any of your contraceptive pills?
reply: Um — yeah, I have a boyfriend. We've been together about a year, just him. I don't think I could be pregnant, and I'm on the pill and I don't miss it.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Whether she could be pregnant

finding: Soft abdomen. Mild suprapubic tenderness. No guarding or rebound. No masses.
No renal angle tenderness on either side.

result: Leucocytes ++, nitrites positive, blood trace, protein trace. hCG not tested.

utterance: I've checked your urine and examined your tummy. It confirms that you have an uncomplicated urinary tract infection (UTI), commonly called cystitis. It hasn't spread to your kidneys, which is good. I will prescribe you an antibiotic called trimethoprim for 3 days to clear it up.
reply: I'm glad it's not serious. I'll take the antibiotics as prescribed. I hope it clears up quickly so I can get back to work.

awards.label: First-line antibiotic: nitrofurantoin 100 mg 6-hourly for 5 days, fosfomycin 3 g once, or trimethoprim 300 mg daily for 3 days

utterance: Please take one tablet of the trimethoprim every night for the next 3 days. It's best taken at night so it stays in your bladder longer. Drink plenty of water. You can use a urinary alkaliser like Ural from the pharmacy, or paracetamol, to help with the stinging while the antibiotics start to work. Also, if you happen to get bad diarrhoea or vomiting from the antibiotics, it can affect your contraceptive pill, so use condoms for 7 days if that happens.
reply: I'll make sure to take it every night. I'll drink lots of water and maybe try the Ural. I'll keep an eye out for any diarrhoea or vomiting and use condoms if needed.

utterance: If your symptoms don't improve after two days on the antibiotics, or if you develop a fever, chills, back pain, or start feeling unwell, please come back to see a doctor right away, as it could mean the infection is moving to your kidneys or we need a different antibiotic.
reply: I'll make sure to come back if it doesn't get better or if I feel worse. Thanks for helping.

utterance: Just to double check, do you have any allergies to any medications, particularly antibiotics like trimethoprim or penicillin?
reply: No, I'm not allergic to anything that I know of.

awards.label: Reasonable differential: Urethritis from a sexually transmitted infection

utterance: Do you have any other questions or concerns before you go?
reply: No, I think that's all. Thanks again.
